- result: The ticket gives its triage, as the method gives it: its kind (kind), its class of change (class), the node at which the work enters, the highest asset it reaches (enters), the node at which it ends (ends), and how much of the system it touches (scope); or it says that the ticket cannot be inducted, and why.

- result: The ticket gives the term that carries its work out (term): one line, "- term: " and then a term in the graph language's written form, either a reference {"term": "reference", "name": "<entry>"} to an entry of the registry this packet lists, or a sequence {"term": "sequence", "terms": [...]} of such references, in the order the work is done.
- result: Proportion is a choice among terms that write the same work: of those, the one in proportion to the work is chosen.
- result: Every word the user wrote in the ticket is unchanged.
- as it stands, the ticket: there; nothing is recorded at it.

- registry: induct-ticket (writes no node; rests on nothing): Triages a ticket as the method does and writes on it the term of registered graph functions that carries its work out, in proportion to it, without changing the user's words. As an entry of a term, naming the stretch it inducts, it fits a later stretch whose right grain cannot be judged until the assets before it are accepted: when the run reaches it, it writes the term for that stretch in its place. Small work never needs one. write-specification (writes intent, product and requirements; rests on nothing): Writes the intent, the product definition and the requirements in one session, for one decision by the user: it fits work that enters at the intent and whose whole specification a person reads and accepts at once, such as a new product of a few commands. write-build (writes design, tests and code; rests on requirements): Writes the design, the tests and the code in one session, judged together by one evaluation and accepted by the user once: it fits work that reaches the design, the tests and the code and that a person judges whole, as a new product of a few commands or a change to one. write-intent (writes intent; rests on nothing): Writes or amends the intent, what is to be built and why, for its own decision by the user: it fits work that enters at the intent and is too large to accept in one decision. write-product (writes product; rests on intent): Writes or amends the product definition, the product's boundary, its terms and what it does within the intent, for its own decision by the user: it fits work that enters at the product definition, and work from the intent too large to accept in one decision. write-requirements (writes requirements; rests on intent and product): Writes or amends the requirements, what the product must do, each under a name of its own, for its own decision by the user: it fits a change that enters at the requirements. write-design (writes design; rests on requirements): Writes or amends the design, how the accepted requirements are met, naming each one, judged on its own: it fits work that enters at the design, and work from the requirements too large to judge whole. write-tests (writes tests; rests on requirements): Writes or amends the tests from the accepted requirements, exercising the product from end to end as a user would, judged before the code is written: it fits work that enters at the tests, and work from the requirements too large to judge whole. write-code (writes code; rests on requirements, design and tests): Writes or amends the code so that it passes the tests and carries out the requirements, judged and accepted on its own: alone, it fits a fault in the code that the accepted requirements and the judged tests already rule out.

- check "the ticket's term composes": yes where the ticket's field term, read from a line "- term: value", is a reference to an entry of the registry listed here, or a sequence of such references, where a reference to induct-ticket is an induction entry that names its stretch, {"term": "reference", "name": "induct-ticket", "enters": "<node>", "ends": "<node>"}, writes the work of that stretch, less than the work it lies in, and is never the term's first entry; the term composes: each entry rests on nodes an entry before it writes, or that are accepted as they now stand and written by no entry of the term, and no node is written twice; it writes exactly the work from the node the field enters names to the node the field ends names: those two nodes and every node that depends on the first and on which the second depends, where the nodes depend so: product on intent; requirements on intent and product; design on requirements; tests on requirements; code on requirements, design and tests; and the vector of its first entry declares an evaluation or a decision.
